name: GoBGP
what_it_is: GoBGP is an open-source BGP implementation written in Go, designed for modern environments with a rich policy engine based on the IETF vendor-neutral model. It exposes a gRPC API for programmatic management and supports a wide range of BGP address families and extensions.
components: gobgp — CLI client for interacting with gobgpd
gRPC API — programmatic management interface (default port 50051)
Prometheus metrics endpoint — exposed via --pprof-host flag, default port 6060, path /metrics
measurement: Prometheus metrics at /metrics (default port 6060) via --pprof-host flag
bgp_peer_state — FSM state (IDLE/CONNECT/ACTIVE/OPENSENT/OPENCONFIRM/ESTABLISHED) and admin state per peer
bgp_routes_received / bgp_routes_accepted / bgp_routes_advertised — per peer and route family
bgp_sent_* / bgp_received_* counters — OPEN, UPDATE, KEEPALIVE, NOTIFICATION, REFRESH, WITHDRAW messages
bgp_peer_flop_count — session flap count per peer
bgp_peer_uptime — time in current FSM state
Grafana dashboard available (dashboard ID 22061-gobgp on grafana.com)
configuration: Config file formats: TOML (default), YAML, JSON, HCL; format specified with -t flag
global.config: AS number, router-id, listen port (default 179), local-address-list
neighbors: peer-as, neighbor-address, local-as, auth-password, passive-mode, ebgp-multihop, route-reflector, add-paths, graceful-restart, afi-safis per neighbor
dynamic-neighbors: accept peers from a prefix range associated with a peer-group
apply-policy: import/export policy with default accept/reject per global RIB or per neighbor
defined-sets: prefix-sets, neighbor-sets, community-sets, ext-community-sets, as-path-sets
policy-definitions: statements with conditions and actions (accept/reject, MED/AS-path/community manipulation)
rpki-servers: RPKI validator address and port for ROV
vrfs: name, RD, RT import/export lists for L3VPN
zebra: FIB integration via UNIX socket, redistribute-route-type-list, version
SIGHUP triggers config reload; -a flag enables auto-reload on file change
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection mechanism documented
Scenario tests use Docker containers (GoBGPContainer, QuaggaBGPContainer, ExaBGPContainer) to simulate multi-peer topologies and test malformed message handling (bgp_malformed_msg_handling_test.py)
Test scenarios cover: graceful restart, long-lived graceful restart, route flap, policy changes, soft reset, BGP confederation edge cases
modes: Route Server mode (route-server-client = true per neighbor)
Route Reflector mode (route-reflector-client = true per neighbor)
Go native library mode (embed GoBGP as a Go package without running gobgpd)
gRPC-only management mode (config file optional; full API control via gRPC)
constraints: No docker-compose file in the repository; scenario tests use Python fabric + Docker SDK to programmatically spin up containers, not docker-compose
BGP listen port defaults to 179 (requires root/CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE); can be overridden to unprivileged port in config
TTL Security and eBGP Multihop are mutually exclusive on the same neighbor
Zebra integration version must match the Quagga/FRR version on the system (version field in config)
Scenario tests require Python 3, Go, and Docker; dependencies installed via pip from test/pip-requires.txt
gRPC default port is 50051; Prometheus/pprof endpoint disabled by default unless --pprof-host is set (--pprof-disable suppresses both unless --metrics-path is explicitly set)
docker_services: No official docker-compose.yml provided in the repository
GoBGPContainer — Go BGP daemon container used in Python scenario tests (test/lib/gobgp.py)
QuaggaBGPContainer — Quagga BGP peer container for interop tests (test/lib/quagga.py)
ExaBGPContainer — ExaBGP peer container for interop tests (test/lib/exabgp.py)
BaGPipe container — used in EVPN/VPN scenario tests (test/lib/bagpipe.py)
BIRD container — used in select interop tests (test/lib/bird.py)
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — multi-container test topology is managed programmatically via Python fabric, not Compose
No built-in traffic generator or route injector beyond gRPC API and CLI
No native NETCONF/YANG or RESTCONF interface (gRPC only for programmatic access)
No web UI or dashboard bundled (Grafana integration is external)
No IS-IS, OSPF, or other IGP support (BGP-only daemon)
